scenes.headline: How a model drafts its own tokens, then checks them
scenes.sub: Uno: speculative decoding with the draft model inside the target.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Byte! Speculative decoding usually needs a second, smaller draft model. Uno deletes it: the drafter is an adapter on the very model that checks it.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: The drafter is a LoRA adapter on the verifier's own frozen backbone. Adapters off gives the target's distribution; adapters on gives a draft.

steps.say: Start with an ordinary autoregressive model, trained as usual, then frozen. That's the verifier.

steps.note: clean rows skip it; noisy rows use it
steps.say: Add a rank one-twenty-eight LoRA adapter to every attention and MLP projection, and train only that, with the backbone frozen.
Each cycle builds a block: the last committed token, then uniformly random token ids. That noise is the literal input.
One forward pass. Clean rows give the verifier's p. Noisy rows go through the adapter, and one denoising step turns noise into a draft, q.
The rejection rule keeps the accepted prefix. Even a total wipeout still emits two tokens: the seed, plus the verifier's own resample.

scenes.title: Why it stays lossless
scenes.text: accept: min(1, p/q)   reject: max(p − q, 0)
scenes.say: The check is ordinary speculative decoding's rule, proved exact in twenty twenty-three.

parts.note: keep the drafted token with this probability
parts.say: Keep the drafted token with probability p over q, capped at one.

parts.note: on rejection, resample from the leftover mass
parts.say: On rejection, resample from where p exceeds q. The output distribution matches the base model's exactly; a bad draft only costs speed.

scenes.title: Speedup over the base model, one H200
scenes.note: the abstract's 'up to 3x' appears in no table
scenes.say: Measured on one H200: two point two times faster at batch one, one point five at batch sixty-four. The abstract's three times appears in no table.

scenes.text: Keep one distribution and add a cheap parallel path to sample from it; the old exactness proof does the rest.

recap: A LoRA adapter drafts on the verifier's own weights
One forward pass yields both p and q
Standard rejection sampling keeps it exact
scenes.say: To recap: one backbone, an adapter that drafts, and a textbook rule that keeps it exact.
